title: Earthy Australian Narutomaki Gyoza
description: A unique, aerated, and earthy twist on a traditional Australian dish featuring narutomaki. This vegetarian-friendly recipe is perfect for a weeknight dinner or special occasion.
instructions: In a large skillet, heat 1 tablespoon of oil over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until translucent, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the cabbage, carrots, and garlic to the skillet and cook for an additional 4-5 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender.
In a large bowl, combine the cooked vegetables, tofu, bush tomato jam, soy sauce (if using), salt, and black pepper. Mix well to combine.
Lay a wonton wrapper on a flat surface and place a tablespoon of the vegetable mixture in the center.
Place a slice of narutomaki on top of the filling, then fold the wrapper into a triangle and press the edges together to seal.
Place the gyoza on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving about 1 inch of space between each gyoza.
Brush the tops of the gyoza with a little water, then sprinkle with salt to taste.
Bake the gyoza in the preheated oven for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown.
Serve the gyoza hot with a side of your choice, such as steamed vegetables or a simple salad.
